title: coverage.json key order depends on PYTHONHASHSEED (byte-nondeterministic output, unhashed)
location: portfolio_engine/python/pe/forensics.py:264 (parent_roles=dict(Counter(ls.roles[p] for p in parents)), parents is a set); written by tools/m2e_build.py:36
evidence: Reran m2e_build from clean output dirs in 5 clones: g2 (random seed), g3 (PYTHONHASHSEED=1), g4 (987654) produced coverage.json that differs in BYTES from the committed file (parent_roles key order OPENING_ONLY/CLOSING_ONLY/MIXED permuted) while json.loads() is equal; g1 happened to match. Only manifests/summary differ otherwise.
repro: cd <clone>; for s in 1 2 3 4; do PYTHONHASHSEED=$s python3 portfolio_engine/tools/m2e_build.py; sha256sum portfolio_engine/reports/m2e_data/*/coverage.json; done
impact: Committed coverage.json is not reproducible byte-for-byte; the file is not in any manifest so the drift is invisible to the manifest tests. Values unaffected (parsed-equal).
proposed_fix: Build parent_roles from sorted keys: dict(sorted(Counter(...).items())); write JSON with sort_keys=True; add coverage.json, case_studies.json and the summaries to the manifest.
proposed_test: Test: run the m2e builders in two subprocesses with different PYTHONHASHSEED and assert byte equality of every output file.

title: Provenance heads in committed manifests do not identify the generating code; run_id depends on git HEAD; dirty check is partial
evidence: Committed m2c manifest: generated_at_head=5b2939ec, working_tree_dirty=true (outputs committed later in 1b0a79f7); m2d: 77521fa7 (committed in f8200e0b); m2e: 10e33962 (final outputs committed in 7117bbce). m2d/m2e manifests carry no dirty flag; m2c dirty check covers only portfolio_engine/python and tools (not cpp, tests, docs, fixtures). provenance.manifest() run_id hashes the git sha, so run_id changes with every commit although inputs/config are identical; git_sha(cwd=dirname(events_path)) reports whichever repo holds the events file or UNAVAILABLE. No C++ binary hash is recorded for implementation=cpp.
impact: A reader cannot rely on generated_at_head to reconstruct the code that produced an artifact. Mitigation VERIFIED: regenerating at current HEAD reproduces all data bytes (only runtime metadata and the unhashed coverage.json order differ).
proposed_fix: Record the code hash (git tree hash of python/, tools/, cpp/) and a full dirty flag in every manifest; exclude the sha from run_id or document it; hash the C++ binary.
proposed_test: Test: provenance.manifest() under two different git shas/dirty states -> same run_id for identical inputs; manifest contains tree hash.

title: Output manifests do not cover every output file; hash bases differ between stages
evidence: manifest_check.py (executed, [INV]): m2c manifest covers 6/8 files (not manifest.json, m2c_summary.json); m2d 6/8 (not m2d_summary.json); m2e per cycle 19/22 (not case_studies.json, coverage.json, manifest.json); m2e_summary.json and review_dispositions.json unhashed. m2c/m2d hash is sha256 of the UNCOMPRESSED text (sha256_of_text; gz bytes are not hashed, gz written with mtime=0 so bytes are reproducible); m2e hashes text and equals file bytes on Linux only because open(...,"w") does not translate newlines on Linux. All 19+19+6+6 listed hashes VERIFIED correct for the committed files; 26 figure CSV hashes verified; PNG hashes are informational.
impact: Summaries that feed the reports (m2c/m2d/m2e summaries, coverage.json) can change without any manifest test failing.
proposed_fix: Hash every file in the output directory (except the manifest) with one stated method (raw bytes); verify in a test.
proposed_test: Test: listdir(output dir) minus manifest.json == manifest file set.

title: Writers use locale-default encoding/newline; ASCII-locale run fails and leaves truncated reports
location: portfolio_engine/tools/m2e_cases.py:65, m2e_catalog.py:32, m2e_coverage_report.py, m2e_build.py:35 (open(path, "w") without encoding/newline)
evidence: g5 clone with PYTHONUTF8=0 PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 LC_ALL=C: m2c, m2d, m2e_build, m2e_charts rc=0 but m2e_cases/m2e_catalog/m2e_coverage_report rc=1 (UnicodeEncodeError for U+2014); the three markdown reports were left missing/empty. Default environment (C.UTF-8 coercion) unaffected. TZ (UTC, Asia/Kolkata, America/New_York) and LC_ALL=C/C.UTF-8 produced identical data bytes (g1-g4).
impact: Non-UTF-8 environments fail; on Windows hashes (computed on "\n" text) would not equal file bytes (SUSPECTED, not run).
proposed_fix: Pass encoding="utf-8", newline="\n" to every open() that writes.
proposed_test: Test: run the report tools with PYTHONUTF8=0 LC_ALL=C.

title: Python and C++ TSV readers accept different token sets; io.hpp claims identical validation
evidence: parse_probe.py (executed): Python accepts and C++ rejects: CRLF files, "+130", " 130", "130 ", "1_30", full-width digits, "+1" side, timestamp 99999999999999999999 (Python unbounded). Lone-CR line endings: Python parses the file, C++ reads one comment line and silently accepts ZERO events (outputs differ). UTF-8 BOM rejected by both. No Python or C++ test covers these. Schema-version check is enforced identically (v2 rejected by both).
impact: No effect on committed data (files are machine-written by write_events and parity is byte-exact on them); a hand-edited or foreign-produced file could be accepted by one engine only.
proposed_fix: Use a strict regex ^-?[0-9]+$ in Python; strip \r or reject it in C++; reject a file with no header and rows; fail if the first non-comment line is absent.
proposed_test: Test: fixtures with CRLF/+/space/underscore tokens must be rejected (or accepted) identically by both engines.

title: Overflow and float-sum semantics differ between engines at extreme magnitudes
location: portfolio_engine/python/pe/ledger.py (no overflow guard) vs cpp/include/pe/ledger.hpp (checked_mul/add); python/pe/invariants.py:27 and lineage_set.py:116 use float sum() (compensated on Python >= 3.12) while cpp sums left to right
evidence: parity_fuzz.py (executed, 245 own random sequences, 1,221 cases): 1,043 byte-identical; 171 cases with quantity*price near/over int64: Python computes exact big ints, C++ rejects with "int64 overflow in P&L arithmetic"; 7 AVG strict-mode cases at q~1e9, px~5e8 paise: Python rejects on cash-identity or episode-realized-sum tolerance, 6 of 7 also rejected by C++, 1 (seed 1151 episode_realized_sums_to_portfolio_realized: -108979214338.08452 vs -108979214341.0) rejected by Python only. Real-ledger magnitude: max |cash| 3.8e8 paise, headroom 2.4e10 x to int64. Outputs identical across Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 (23 hashes).
impact: None for real data. The parity statements hold on the domain |q*px| << 9e18; outside it the engines differ in behaviour (C++ fails safe).
proposed_fix: Document the domain; add an overflow guard or Python check mirroring C++; replace sum() over floats by an explicit loop in invariants/lineage_set; make AVG tolerance relative to intermediate magnitudes.
proposed_test: Test: q=3e9, px=3e9 sequence must raise in both engines.

title: Dependencies unpinned; reproducibility asserted only for the present environment
evidence: Python core (ledger, replay, lineage, lineage_set, invariants, closing_batches, wing_body, cases, tsvio, provenance) imports stdlib only (AST scan, VERIFIED); pandas (3.0.5) + pyarrow (26.0.1) are needed by generators/historical.py and forensics.py; matplotlib 3.11.2 by tools/m2e_charts.py (PNG bytes identical to committed under this version only); numpy/pandas by older tools; `market_data` (external) by select_demo_cycles.py. Core outputs identical under Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 (VERIFIED, 23 hashes). Float sum() over floats exists only in invariants.py:27 / lineage_set.py:116 (check paths; do not enter outputs).
impact: A different pandas/matplotlib version may change generator input handling or PNG bytes (SUSPECTED).
proposed_fix: Add a lock/requirements file and record versions in manifests.
proposed_test: CI job on the pinned versions.

title: Inconsistent schema versioning across files
evidence: Only events carry schema_version (pe.fill.v1) and the dump carries "#PE_STATE_DUMP v1". Lineage TSVs, parents.tsv, m2d links/items have no version field/header; m2c has grouping_version CB1; m2e manifest version M2E_1; m2d manifest none. SCHEMAS.md retains superseded draft sections (allocations.tsv, lifecycle terminal_status, wing_body.tsv) with "supersedes" notes. Shared column constants are duplicated in Python and C++ headers (kEventColumns etc.), kept consistent only by parity tests.
impact: A consumer cannot detect a layout change by version.
proposed_fix: Add a version comment line/field to every shared file.
proposed_test: Test: every output file declares a schema version matched to SCHEMAS.md.
